title: Construction-Era Load and Credit on the FloodGuard Building Premium
content:
Underwriting training note — FloodGuard Private Flood Policy renewal offers and the year a building was built.

The FloodGuard Private Flood Policy applies a construction-era adjustment to the building premium at the renewal offer, following the year built shown on the customer's HomeGuard Homeowners Policy in force at the same property address as the flood policy.

## Rule

A building built before 1975 carries a load of 10 percent as a surcharge on the building premium; a building built in or after 2000 carries a credit of 5 percent as a reduction of the building premium; and a building built in between, or one with no HomeGuard policy in force at the same property address, carries no construction-era adjustment.

## Questions answered

Which record decides the year built? The year built on the customer's HomeGuard Homeowners Policy that is in force at the same property address as the FloodGuard policy.

Which buildings carry the 10 percent surcharge? Those whose HomeGuard policy in force at the same address shows a year built before 1975, for example 1974 or 1962.

Which buildings carry the 5 percent reduction? Those whose HomeGuard policy in force at the same address shows a year built of 2000 or later, for example 2000 or 2011.

What about a building built from 1975 through 1999? No construction-era adjustment.

What if the customer holds no HomeGuard policy in force at that address? No construction-era adjustment, whatever the building's age.

## Boundary years

| Year built on the HomeGuard policy in force at the same address | Adjustment |
|---|---|
| 1974 | Surcharge of 10 percent |
| 1975 | None |
| 1999 | None |
| 2000 | Reduction of 5 percent |
| No HomeGuard policy in force at the same address | None |

Hypothetical figures: a building premium of 500.00 with the surcharge is 550.00; with the reduction it is 475.00.
